newsitem.title: FRANCE: Stabbed French minister will miss Cannes festival.
newsitem.headline: Stabbed French minister will miss Cannes festival.

text.p: French Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy, stabbed by a knife-wielding assailant on Friday, will be in hospital, or convalescing, for two weeks and will miss next week's inauguration of the Cannes film festival, doctors said on Saturday.
Douste-Blazy was attacked on Friday while on an election campaign trip to his constituency at Lourdes, southwestern France, where he is mayor.
Doctors said suffered two broken ribs and a lung wound and will stay at least two more days in an intensive care unit.
Education Minister Francois Bayrou who visited his colleague in hospital said Douste-Blazy was as well as could be but in some shock.
A 37-year-old man of Albanian origin, Adlal Cifti, was placed under investigation for premeditated attempted murder.
Court sources said Cifti, who was under psychiatric treatement, denied guilt. They said Cifti attacked Douste-Blazy with a screwdriver in 1992.
